lessons.title: Variables, Data Types & Arrays
body: Declare variables using const (for fixed values) and let (for values that change). Avoid using var in modern development.
The core data types are: number, string, boolean, null, undefined, object, and array. You can check a type using the typeof operator.
Arrays are an analyst's most powerful tool: use map to transform data, filter to select specific items, and reduce to aggregate totals.
Example: const cleanData = data.filter((x) => x.value != null).map((x) => x.value);

quiz.q: Which array method is the best choice for calculating a total sum?
options: map
filter
reduce
forEach
quiz.explain: The reduce method folds an array down into a single value, making it perfect for calculating totals and averages.

quiz.q: What does the expression 'typeof null' return in JavaScript?
options: "null"
"object"
"undefined"
"boolean"
quiz.explain: 'typeof null' returns 'object'. This is a historical bug in JavaScript that every analyst simply needs to memorize.

lessons.title: Lab: Calculate Total Sales
body: Write a function named solve(input) that accepts an array of numbers and returns their total sum.
Your function must ignore any values that are not numbers (such as null, undefined, or strings).
Example: solve([10, null, 20]) should return 30.

cv-siap-lamar.title: Build a One-Page CV Ready for Applications

lessons.title: Structuring a CV for a 30-Second HR Review
body: Keep it to one page for fresh graduates. Include: your name, contact info, professional headline, education, experience, and skills.
Highlight numbers and results, not just generic traits. Writing “Managed Rp5M/day in cash flow with zero variances” is much stronger than “Hardworking and diligent.”
Use a professional, recent photograph and a sensible email address (your actual name, no nicknames).

quiz.q: How long should a fresh graduate's CV be?
options: One page
Two pages
Three pages
As long as necessary — more detail is better
quiz.explain: HR recruiters scan dozens of CVs rapidly. One dense, highly relevant page is always better than three pages of fluff.

quiz.q: Which of these bullet points would impress a recruiter the most?
options: Honest, hardworking, and a good team player.
Managed Rp5M/day in cash flow over 6 months with zero variances.
Possess relevant experience in the field.
Capable of working well under pressure.
quiz.explain: Recruiters look for numbers, specific durations, and verifiable results. Generic personality traits without proof are usually ignored.

lessons.title: Setting Up Your Public Portfolio: superbright.id/u/you
body: Recruiters will almost always click your portfolio link. At a minimum, include: 1 completed project, 1 verified certificate, and a clear list of skills.
When describing a project, use the Problem → Action → Result format.
Keep your profile active. Update it every time you finish a new learning path, not just once a year when you apply for a job.

quiz.q: What is the most effective way to structure a project description?
options: Problem → Action → Result
Result → Action → Problem
Action → Problem → Result
Write a simple, unstructured summary
quiz.explain: The Problem provides necessary context, the Action demonstrates your skills, and the Result proves the real-world impact of your work.

quiz.q: What is the minimum requirement for an effective public portfolio profile?
options: 1 completed project + 1 verified certificate + a clear skills list
A highly professional headshot
A detailed personal biography and life motto
A comprehensive list of your personal hobbies
quiz.explain: Recruiters need to verify your capability within 60 seconds. They look for tangible projects, certifications, and concrete skills.

interview-pertama.title: Handling Your First HR Interview Without Panic

lessons.title: Answering “Tell Me About Yourself” in Under 2 Minutes
body: Use the Present → Past → Proof → Future framework: start with who you are now, briefly touch on your background, highlight one major achievement, and explain why you want this specific role.
Do not simply read your CV out loud — the recruiter already has it. Provide context and stories that aren't on the paper.
Practice with a timer until your answer lands consistently around the 2-minute mark.

quiz.q: What is the best structural flow for a professional self-introduction?
options: Present → Past → Proof → Future (Target Role)
Target Role → Proof → Past → Present
Past → Present → Target Role → Proof
A detailed chronological timeline starting from high school
quiz.explain: Opening with your current status grounds the conversation, and closing with your target shows clear alignment with the role you are interviewing for.

quiz.q: What is the ideal length for your initial self-introduction?
options: Around 2 minutes
Around 10 minutes
As quickly as possible
Keep talking until the interviewer interrupts
quiz.explain: Two minutes gives you enough time to cover the key points without losing the interviewer's attention.

lessons.title: Handling Salary Expectations & Trick Questions
body: Always research market salary rates for similar roles in your specific city before the interview.
When asked about salary, provide a flexible range (e.g., “Based on my research, 7–9 million, but I am open to discussing the total package”), rather than demanding a fixed number.
When asked “What is your greatest weakness?”, provide a real, operational weakness and immediately explain the steps you are actively taking to improve it.

quiz.q: What is the most professional way to state your salary expectations?
options: Provide a salary range based on current market research.
State the absolute highest number you can think of to anchor the negotiation.
Say “I will accept whatever the standard company policy is.”
Refuse to answer until you are officially offered the job.
quiz.explain: Providing a researched range shows you understand the market value of the role while remaining flexible and collaborative.

quiz.q: How should you answer the “What is your greatest weakness?” question?
options: Say “I'm a perfectionist” but offer no real examples.
Share a genuine professional weakness and explain how you are working to overcome it.
Confidently state that you do not have any relevant weaknesses.
List several major personal flaws to demonstrate complete honesty.
quiz.explain: Recruiters use this question to assess your self-awareness and your ability to learn and grow (growth mindset), not to find a perfect candidate.

lessons.title: Finding Where Your Customers Actually Are
body: In Indonesia, SME customers are primarily active on Shopee, TikTok, and WhatsApp. Pick ONE primary channel and focus all your initial effort there.
Authentic photos of your actual products perform much better than generic stock photos. Customers buy from brands they feel are honest and real.
Consistency beats going viral. Posting one good piece of content every day for 30 days will yield far better long-term results than one massive viral hit.

quiz.q: What is the best initial marketing strategy for a small SME team with limited resources?
options: Focus entirely on optimizing one single channel for the first 30 days.
Create accounts on every major social platform to maximize reach.
Spend the entire budget on ads immediately to get fast results.
Wait until you can afford to hire a dedicated social media manager.
quiz.explain: A single, highly active and optimized channel will always generate more trust and sales than five neglected accounts.

quiz.q: What type of visual content generates the most trust among SME customers?
options: Authentic photos and videos showing the real products and processes.
Highly polished, aesthetic stock photography.
Motivational quotes formatted nicely.
Trending internet memes.
quiz.explain: Consumers value transparency. Showing the real product, the real packaging process, and the real owners builds the necessary trust to make a sale.

lessons.title: Launching Your First Rp50K Ad Campaign
body: One ad should have one clear goal: generating inbound WhatsApp inquiries. Do not run ads just for 'likes' or 'followers'.
Start by targeting customers within your immediate city radius, rather than blasting your ad across the whole country.
Monitor your 'cost per inquiry'. If an ad is running for 3 days and losing money, turn it off immediately and test a new photo or caption.

quiz.q: What is the most important success metric for an SME's first advertising campaign?
options: The cost to acquire one inbound customer inquiry.
The total number of likes the ad receives.
The number of new followers gained during the campaign.
The volume of positive comments left on the post.
quiz.explain: Customer inquiries lead directly to sales. Vanity metrics like 'likes' do not help pay for business expenses.

quiz.q: When is the right time to shut down a poorly performing ad?
options: After 3 consecutive days with no inbound inquiries or sales.
After 1 hour if it hasn't gone viral.
Never turn it off early; wait until the entire budget is spent.
After 30 days of continuous running.
quiz.explain: Running an ad for three days provides enough data to judge if the creative is working, preventing you from wasting a small budget on a bad ad.

lessons.title: Adapting the 50-30-20 Rule for Independent Living
body: The standard rule is 50% for needs (rent, groceries, transport), 30% for wants, and 20% for savings. Adapt these percentages to fit your reality, don't just memorize them.
Pay yourself first: set up an automatic transfer (autodebit) to move your 20% into savings on payday. Do not wait to see what is left at the end of the month.
Your emergency fund target should be 3 to 6 times your monthly living expenses, and it must be kept in a separate account from your daily spending.

quiz.q: When is the most effective time to transfer money into your savings account?
options: Automatically on payday via an autodebit setup.
At the end of the month, using whatever money is leftover.
Only when you receive an annual bonus or extra income.
Manually, whenever you happen to remember.
quiz.explain: Relying on 'leftover' money usually results in saving nothing. Automating the transfer ensures you prioritize your financial security before spending.

quiz.q: What is a healthy and secure target for an emergency fund?
options: 3 to 6 times your total monthly living expenses.
Exactly 50% of one month's salary.
A flat rate of Rp1 million is sufficient.
Emergency funds aren't necessary if you have access to credit cards or paylater apps.
quiz.explain: A three-month reserve gives you enough runway to handle emergencies like medical bills or sudden unemployment without falling into high-interest debt.

lessons.title: Identifying Online Scams and Illegal Lending
body: Legitimate lending institutions are strictly registered with the OJK. Always verify a lender against the official OJK registry before applying, regardless of how professional their ads look.
Never, under any circumstances, share an OTP code with anyone. This includes callers who claim to be from your bank, the police, or a digital wallet provider.
If you receive a suspicious or unexpected fund transfer, do not forward the money to another account. Verify the Virtual Account (VA), contact the bank officially, and file a report. Stay calm.

quiz.q: What is the most important step to take before borrowing money from an online platform?
options: Verify that the company is officially registered and supervised by the OJK.
Check if their social media advertisements look professional and trustworthy.
Read positive reviews and testimonials on their Instagram page.
Confirm that they are offering a 0% introductory interest rate.
quiz.explain: Illegal lenders often use harassment and intimidation to collect debts. Checking the OJK registry is your first and most important line of defense.

quiz.q: You receive a phone call from someone claiming to be your bank, asking you to read them an OTP code sent to your phone. What should you do?
options: Hang up immediately, and if concerned, call the bank yourself using their official customer service number.
Give them the code, assuming they already have access to your account data.
Ask them to hold the line while you quickly transfer your funds to a safe account.
Block the number but take no further action to verify.
quiz.explain: Legitimate banks and financial institutions will never ask you to read an OTP code over the phone. Always verify through official channels.

lessons.title: Understanding Corporate Hierarchy and Communication
body: Communicate proactively: sending a brief progress update in the afternoon is always better than waiting for your manager to ask, or delivering a panicked report when a deadline is missed.
If assigned an impossible workload, respond professionally: “Understood. To ensure quality, which of these deadlines should I prioritize first?” Do not simply stay silent and fail.
Deliver constructive criticism privately and always bring a potential solution. Deliver praise openly and publicly.

quiz.q: Your manager assigns you a new task that makes it impossible to hit today's existing deadlines. What is the most professional response?
options: Acknowledge the task, explain the time constraint, and ask them to clarify which item is the top priority.
Accept the task silently, then work unapproved overtime trying to finish everything.
Refuse the new task bluntly, stating you are already at maximum capacity.
Quietly forward one of your existing tasks to a coworker.
quiz.explain: Managers need accurate information to make decisions. Providing data on your workload helps them reprioritize effectively without causing unnecessary drama.

quiz.q: What is the most professional way to give critical feedback to a colleague?
options: In a private 1-on-1 setting, while also suggesting a possible solution.
In the main team WhatsApp group so everyone is aware.
Casually during a team lunch or coffee break.
By posting a vague complaint on your social media status.
quiz.explain: Praising in public builds morale, but criticizing in private preserves professional dignity. Offering solutions shows you are collaborative, not just complaining.

lessons.title: Meeting Etiquette and Handling Feedback
body: Arrive at meetings 5 minutes early, bring your notes, and prepare at least one thoughtful question. This simple habit forms a huge part of how your professionalism is judged.
When receiving critical feedback, use this framework: Listen actively → Ask for specific examples → Commit to an improvement plan.
Understand generational differences in the office: senior staff often value procedural correctness and respect, while junior teams value speed and agility. Adapt your communication style accordingly.

quiz.q: Which behavior during a meeting leaves the best impression on management?
options: Arriving a few minutes early, reviewing your notes, and asking a relevant, prepared question.
Arriving exactly on time but having no prior preparation.
Bringing coffee or snacks for the whole team to build rapport.
Making sure you sit at the very front of the room.
quiz.explain: Asking a relevant question proves that you have reviewed the material in advance and are actively engaged in the team's objectives.

quiz.q: You receive harsh but fair criticism from your supervisor. What is the best way to respond?
options: Listen carefully, ask for a concrete example so you understand fully, and outline how you will fix it.
Immediately defend your actions to prove you were not entirely at fault.
Become visibly upset and ask to take the rest of the day off.
Respond by pointing out a mistake your supervisor made recently.
quiz.explain: Asking for concrete examples turns an emotional or difficult conversation into a practical discussion based on actionable data you can improve.
